title: St. Louis City 3-2 Los Angeles FC: Damet's side clinch first-ever playoff win
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutSt. Louis City 3-2 Los Angeles FC: Damet's side clinch first-ever playoff winShareAfter navigating their way through a nervy ending at Energizer Park, St. Louis City recorded their maiden MLS playoff victory.St. Louis City clinched their first-ever MLS Cup playoff win after defeating Los Angeles FC 3-2 in Game 1 of their Round One series.

Daniel Edelman and Jeong Sang-bin fired the hosts into a 2-0 lead at Energizer Park, and though Sergi Palencia pulled a goal back for LAFC, Simon Becher rendered Denis Bouanga's late penalty a consolation.

Rafael Navarro squandered an early chance, curling wide of the right post from inside the box, but made up for it in the 34th minute as he teed up Edelman for a first-time finish into the bottom-left corner.
Jeong then doubled City's lead early in the second half, drilling low past Hugo Lloris from the edge of the box after LAFC failed to clear their lines from a corner.
Palencia scored a brilliant header just after the hour to halve the visitors' deficit, but Becher came off the bench to volley in a third for St. Louis.

LAFC did set up a nervy finish after Bouanga netted from the penalty spot in the 85th minute, following a handball from Chris Durkin, but after Son Heung-min curled over from a free-kick in stoppage time, Sergio Vasquez missed a sitter in the six-yard box after a pinpoint cross from Tommy Mihalic.
No matter how the 2026 season ends for Yoann Damet's side, it will be a campaign the St. Louis faithful will never forget.

Heading into the postseason, St. Louis had already set an MLS record 20-game unbeaten run across all competitions, which saw them clinch a play-off spot after finishing 14th in the Western Conference last season.
Though their stunning run came to an end in October, they then defeated the Columbus Crew on penalties to win the US Open Cup – the club's first-ever silverware.
St. Louis have now recorded their first-ever playoff win, which comes after a poor run of form in the league.
City lost four of their last five regular-season games (W1), and top scorer Becher did not net in any of those matches, but ended his scoring duck at a vital moment.

LAFC can take some positives, edging the expected goals (xG) battle 2.03 to 1.4 and conceding two long-range strikes, but Xavier Tamarit's side now have no room for error in this best-of-three series.
